thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: us-west-2 continuous-batching latency & paging surge detected. burst_evictions=1.9k/min, cont-batch tail p99=4.2s, paging_errors ++. alert_id=2141002345

ryan-oncall: picking this up. first look at dashboards: sudden jump aligns with a config push ~30m ago. any rollout notes?

emily-runtime: I see a merge from eng-ml that increased `max_num_seqs` from 8 -> 64 and also increased `batch_timeout_ms` from 50 -> 250. that combination lets batches wait longer and merge many sequences -> larger merged batches, more unique KV keys per merged batch.

tanya-sre: paging pressure leads to eviction storms and then retries - observed request amplification. customers hit high tail latencies. need rapid mitigation.

ryan-oncall: mitigation options: 1) force default `batch_timeout_ms=75` 2) roll back `max_num_seqs` to 8 3) enable per-model soft cap on merged-batch token count. which is fastest?

emily-runtime: fastest is to set `batch_timeout_ms` low (control-plane quickpatch) and simultaneously set `max_num_seqs=12` as a partial rollback to limit seq explosion.

deploy-bot: issuing patch dpl-2141002400 -> applying canary to 3 pods in us-west-2.

analytics: synthetic traffic started against canary. merged-batch size p50 dropped 3.2k -> 480 tokens, evictions/min down 1.9k -> 140 within 70s. paging errors trending down.

customer-success: notified top affected customers (DataMart, LogiBank). DataMart confirms generated responses are back to normal latency.

ryan-oncall: promoting to full roll. deploy-bot: rollout progress 0/30 -> 18/30 -> 30/30.

emily-runtime: making immediate runtime guard: reject config updates that set `max_num_seqs` > 32 or `batch_timeout_ms` > 200ms without explicit safety flag. pushing schema change to control-plane.

tanya-sre: adding an alert for "merged-batch token count p99 > 100k" and "unique KV keys/min > 10k". also adding runbook step to check recent batching config PRs on paging alerts.

ryan-oncall: short impact summary: incident caused by unsafe increase in `max_num_seqs` combined with longer `batch_timeout_ms` allowing oversized merged batches, which increased KV cache key diversity and triggered an eviction cascade and paging spikes. customer impact: elevated latency for some endpoints in us-west-2 for ~25 minutes, mitigated after quickpatch.

emily-runtime: follow-ups: 1) add unit/regression test that simulates config combos to measure projected KV key growth 2) add telemetry for merged-batch hold time distribution 3) update onboarding PR checklist for batching-related config changes 4) postmortem and blame-free retro. opening tickets now.

deploy-bot: deploys complete, dpl-2141002400 closed.

analytics: final metrics: evictions/min baseline was ~30, peaked to 1900, back to 45. p99 latency peaked 4.2s, now 350ms. paging error rate returned to baseline.

customer-success: LogiBank will request a formal post-incident writeup; cc'ing account team.

ryan-oncall: handing off to emily-runtime for RCA and follow-ups. emily, please update this thread with ticket numbers and PR links.

emily-runtime: ack. created tickets: BATCH-1023 (guardrail schema), BATCH-1024 (regression tests), BATCH-1025 (telemetry). PRs: control-plane schema PR #4812, runtime-reject PR #4813. will post links when merged.

incident-bot: INCIDENT SUMMARY: root cause = simultaneous increases to `max_num_seqs` and `batch_timeout_ms` enabling oversized merged batches -> KV cache churn -> paging/eviction cascade -> latency cliff. mitigation = lowered `batch_timeout_ms`, reduced `max_num_seqs` to safer level, runtime guard and alerts added. impact = elevated latency & retries for subset of customers in us-west-2 for ~25m. follow-ups assigned to runtime and SRE.

ryan-oncall: closing active mitigation; thread remains open for postmortem. thanks team. :white_check_mark:
